about.title: about
about.paragraph_1: every curl, every acanthus leaf, every rosette is already a ready-made symbol of elegant restriction. it is “beautiful censorship” in its purest form. assembling an angel from them performs an alchemy of meanings: the language of separation—bars, grilles, gates—is transformed into the language of protective sanctity. the fence’s severity is visually softened and translated into the register of sacred beauty, yet its essence—restriction—remains. today, angels guard not the gardens of eden but the borders of digital and physical domains.
about.paragraph_2: in internet space, the angel has long ceased to be a religious symbol and become a cultural simulacrum: in messengers, social networks, and avatars. new physical angels assembled from fence elements materialise these digital simulacra. they objectify the digital aesthetics of security. their wings, made from forged curls, are a metaphor for the “wings” of social-media privacy settings: an illusion of flight and freedom that is technically a complex system of filters and restrictions.
